contribution.position: I hold my earlier position. I am answering qa's claim on axis:risk that peak_memory is 380MB and comfortably inside the 512MB budget. That figure does not appear in artifact:perf-report, which records 740MB at peak load against a 512MB budget, about 45% over. Unless qa has a different measurement that is not in the artifact list, the 'risk is contained' conclusion rests on a number the record doesn't support. I also looked at product's cost claim for something new. artifact:cost-sheet gives +3% against a 5% ceiling, but it does not say whether that figure assumes the current 512MB limit or a raised one. If the memory budget is revised to fit 740MB, the cost margin may shrink. That is a gap in the record, not evidence of overrun. ops's reliance on artifact:ops-runbook still shows only that recovery is documented, not that the failure is prevented. artifact:incident-log shows two retry-storm sev2s last quarter, which is the failure mode an OOM-and-retry loop would trigger. The artifact list has no load test at the production memory limit and no confirmation of retry backoff or caps. Those are what would change my view, along with a cost-sheet figure tied to the memory limit that would actually be deployed.
